title: What is known about 1RB---_0RC0RE_1RD1RF_1LE0LB_1RC0LD_1RC1RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB---_0RC0RE_1RD1RF_1LE0LB_1RC0LD_1RC1RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The run is a sequence of phases: a counter n becomes 8·(n div 3) + d, where the residue of n mod 3 and a word P of blocks to its left decide d and the next word. Lean proves the rounds of a phase for all lengths, and the residue-0 phase end: (L 0 1a+1 0, 3m + 3) → (L 0, a + 8m + 11). No halting transition was found in the word dynamics (trusted, by simulation), so the machine may well run forever, but the word dynamics is unbounded and not understood.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (A1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 76,311 cells have been visited and 46,473 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.505).

claims.title: The rounds of a phase
claims.text: The start of a phase, one round (three 1s of the counter become four pairs 01), and any number of rounds at once, for every count and every word P, and a whole phase for residue 0: a word ending in a block 0 1^(a+1) 0 and n = 3m + 3 give the word without that block and n = a + 8m + 11.

claims.title: The phase map agrees with the machine
claims.text: At all 8 transitions between the 9 phase starts of the first 4·10<sup>8</sup> steps (the last at step 332,166,746, n = 39,016) the measured word map predicts the next phase start.

claims.title: No halt in the explored word dynamics
claims.text: Exploring the word dynamics breadth first for every sequence of residues (600 words, the longest 43 cells): no transition halts, and every one returns to a phase start.

claims.title: The real orbit
claims.text: From the first phase start (step 110, P = 1111110, n = 12), computed exactly: no halt in 2,000 phases (n then has 2,835 bits); 20 distinct words, the longest 17 cells, and the word keeps returning to empty.

claims.title: Probably nonhalting, for a structural reason not yet proved
claims.text: Unlike Antihydra-type machines, no halting word is known here, so there is no coin-flip argument for a halt. The word behaves like a stack of nested counters (a residue-0 phase absorbs its last block into the counter, the others push or edit blocks), and the explored part of it never halts; a proof would need an invariant on all reachable words.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: It halts if and only if the word dynamics, driven by the residues mod 3 of the counter, reaches a halting word. None is known; proving that none is reachable needs an invariant for an unbounded word.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. A counter grows by a factor of about 8/3 each phase, and its residues mod 3 edit a word of blocks on the tape. No halting word has been found, which points to nonhalting, but the words reachable are unbounded.

facts.text: per phase: the rounds of a phase are proved in Lean for every count.
of the word dynamics explored for every residue sequence: no halt.
No halt in the C simulator; 76,311 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.

sections.heading: Phases: a counter and a word
html: Stop the machine every time the head, in state C, is at the right end of the tape with the tape reading

a word P (ending in 0), a block of n 1s and the fixed end 0. During a phase the head goes back and forth between the counter and the right end: each round takes three 1s from the counter and writes four pairs 01 at the right (Lean, for all counts). When fewer than three 1s are left, the residue n mod 3 decides what happens: the head goes on into P and edits its last blocks, and on the way back the pairs become the next counter. So n becomes 8·(n div 3) + d, where d and the next word depend only on P and n mod 3.

In the words, a residue-0 phase absorbs the last block of P into the counter (proved in Lean for the machines with factor 8/3), while the other residues push new blocks or edit the last ones, often through a smaller phase of the same kind run on a block of P. So P is a stack of nested counters.

sections.heading: Does any word halt?
html: The word map was measured by simulation (each pair of a word and a residue is run from three sample counts, which must agree). Exploring the word dynamics breadth first for every sequence of residues (600 words, the longest 43 cells): no transition halts, and every one returns to a phase start.

From the first phase start (step 110, P = 1111110, n = 12), computed exactly: no halt in 2,000 phases (n then has 2,835 bits); 20 distinct words, the longest 17 cells, and the word keeps returning to empty.

So, unlike Antihydra-type machines, there is no known halting word and no probabilistic argument for a halt: the machine is plausibly nonhalting. A proof would need a description of every word the dynamics can reach, closed under all residues, together with the phase ends proved in Lean for each kind of word. That was not done here.

Related machines. 1RB---_0RC0RE_1RD1RF_1LE0LB_1RC0LD_1RC1RA and 1RB0LC_1RC1RE_1LA0LD_0RB0RA_1RB1RF_1RD--- are the same table with the states relabelled (no mirror), started in different states: their phase rules, word maps and Lean files are the same up to the name of the phase state (C and B), and only their orbits differ. 1RB---_1RC1RE_1LD0LE_1RF0LC_0RD0RA_0RB1RD has the same kind of phase, with factor 10/3 instead of 8/3.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.505).
After 109 steps the tape spans 76,311 cells (13 left of the start, 59,647 right), with a density of 1s of 0.609.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A counter n multiplied by about 8/3 per phase, whose residue mod 3 edits a word P of blocks on the tape; no halting word found (a Collatz-type word dynamics, open).
